text: By government decision, legislative amendments will be prepared regarding the recognition of diplomas issued before 2010

According to the decision of the Georgian government, legislative amendments will be submitted to the Parliament, based on which thousands of citizens will be able to resolve problems related to the recognition of diplomas issued before 2010, - stated the Minister of Education, Science and Youth of Georgia, Givi Mikanadze.
As the minister noted, according to the change, 4-year full-time and 5-year part-time studies will be recognized equally.

He said that the change will affect students who enrolled in a recognized university and completed their studies in an unrecognized regime, as well as citizens who were enrolled in a university before educational institutions obtained a license.

"We had this situation - our citizens took exactly the same number of subjects in a 4-year program and received the same qualification as in a 5-year part-time program. According to the previous legislation, a 5-year program was equivalent to a master's degree, and a 4-year program was awarded a bachelor's degree. Based on the changes, those who completed a 4-year program will receive a diploma equivalent to a master's degree, which will significantly facilitate the employment of citizens in their desired field.

Until 2010, when a unified system was established, there was no register in the education sector that would ensure the information of students. There were cases when specific universities that were not accredited did not inform applicants about this and enrolled them anyway. Later, when they issued a diploma, graduates had problems recognizing this document.

In addition, a number of higher education institutions had authorization for a certain period of time and then had it terminated during the study period. Students were not informed about this either, and these university graduates subsequently had problems.

"The presented legislative amendments will finally put an end to the long, problematic processes that our citizens go through to get their diplomas recognized - going to court, appealing the processes, which are time-consuming and effort-consuming. All this will once and for all be history, and the diplomas of thousands of our citizens will be recognized," said Givi Mikanadze.
